You are the cold reviewer in the initiative-check process, step screen, round 2 (fresh context; you have seen nothing before). Read only the two files named here — nothing else.

- criteria_path: /home/vscode/rebaseline/basis/fitness/initiative.fitness.md
- initiative: /home/vscode/rebaseline/initiatives/init-request-routing.md

Step prompt (verbatim): "State, as judge_stamp, the model and prompt version you judge as. Read the criteria set at criteria_path and the initiative at initiative — nothing else. Judge the initiative against every scenario. Report every finding with the criterion it fails by name, the quoted text, the change, and whether you could decide it (confident) or not (wobbly); for a wobbly finding quote the whole passage, since the authority decides from the review. A defect no criterion names is a finding with criterion "uncovered". Verdict "clean" only if there are no findings; otherwise "findings" with the top three changes."

Return exactly this structure:
judge_stamp: <model id> / screen prompt v5
verdict: clean | findings
findings:
- criterion: <scenario name or number, or "uncovered">
  section: <which section of the initiative>
  quoted: "<the text>"
  change: <what would repair it>
  decided: confident | wobbly
top_three: <the three most important changes, or "none">

Be literal to the scenarios. Do not invent criteria. Do not read any other file.

# Initiative: Request routing and the small-change lane

## Framing

Originator (product authority, 2026-09-04, through the lead shop's
operational contract, which has no artifact yet (lead-4kymc);
discovery lead-1kp6m): "this is about getting simple
things done, which now requires being able to route requests." "we
don't have a good entry-point to go from open-ended human input to
something an agent can work with."

Problem: a simple, functional change can only get done through the
full product flow, whose stages protect a bet the change does not
spend; and an ask arising in conversation has no record until a
discovery conversation opens for it. Outcome: every ask is recorded on
arrival and has a decided route — into discovery, to a simple change,
or declined with the authority — and a simple change reaches a
verified result without the stages that protect a bet.

## For whom

The product authority and anyone bringing the lead shop an ask.
Measure: a simple functional change — the originator's example, a
related-to entry on the decision brief — reaches a verified result
through a recorded, routed ask, the full flow untouched. Now 0: the
only door is discovery, the only path the full flow. Target 1.
Interaction type: conversational.

## Appetite

One working session of the lead shop, covering every ask recorded
and routed on arrival, the route into discovery kept open, and the
example change verified: definitions alone do not meet the measure. No-gos, reasoned:

- The configuration lane (lead-1d0eo): no new types this session.
- Grooming of all open work (lead-izfpk): ordering, not doing.
- Draining the register pileup (lead-vx02q): work of its own.
- The Framing-refinement rule (lead-ghulb): not needed to route.
- New artifact types — the authority's direction: "we are not working
  through any new types".
- The bet and the screen of record: they protect an appetite a simple
  change does not spend.

## Feasibility and usability

Feasible; the verified run is the risk. No contract exists on this
branch; the repository's two features (both lead-shop-owned) touch
neither requests nor routing: no conflict. Each piece amends a lead-shop
definition: `request` gains a producing intake process, the feature
typedef's framing link admits a request, discovery's `topic` input and
the initiative admit one, the decision brief's closed field set gains
related-to. The definitions fit one session; the example change
delivered and verified through the new lane may not. (architect,
2026-09-04)

Hypothesis, no observed use: "make a request" becomes a core-task entry
holding on every type — options: state the ask in the originator's
words; see the request's id; see its route (discovery, small lane,
declined) and reason. The conversational door is an assistant
interaction: the router says the route before acting, and the person
can correct it (`control-stays-with-the-person`). (designer,
2026-09-04)

## Decomposition

None: no Bounded Context is touched. Every amended definition and the
example change sit in the lead shop's tree; no contract exists on this
branch to rely on. Cross-context flow: none.

## Features

None yet.

verdict: findings
findings:
- criterion: 4 — the problem, not the solution
  section: For whom
  quoted: "Measure: a simple functional change — the originator's example, a related-to entry on the decision brief — reaches a verified result through a recorded, routed ask, the full flow untouched."
  change: "a related-to entry on the decision brief" names a structure (a field on a named artifact) inside a section scenario 4 parses; either name the example as a what ("the originator's example simple change", with the concrete instance carried in Feasibility, which scenario 4 does not parse) or the authority rules the example instance a what and records it.
  decided: wobbly
- criterion: 4 — the problem, not the solution
  section: Framing
  quoted: "\"we don't have a good entry-point to go from open-ended human input to something an agent can work with.\""
  change: "entry-point" reads as an interface form; the criteria set's own history (2026-09-04) rules no exemption for the originator's quoted words and that the framer's wording changes. Either keep the first quote only ("this is about getting simple things done, which now requires being able to route requests") and carry the second in the Document History, or the authority rules "entry-point" a what.
  decided: wobbly
- criterion: 1 — the framing is complete and in the originator's words
  section: Framing
  quoted: "Originator (product authority, 2026-09-04, through the lead shop's operational contract, which has no artifact yet (lead-4kymc); discovery lead-1kp6m):"
  change: the contract the intent entered through is named as one that does not exist as an artifact. A cold reader cannot decide whether "names the contract" is met by naming an absent one. State the contract as it stands today (e.g., "the authority's direct conversation with the lead-pm, recorded in the discovery conversation lead-1kp6m") or the authority accepts the absent contract as the named one.
  decided: wobbly
- criterion: 3 — appetite bounded, no-gos reasoned
  section: Appetite
  quoted: "- The configuration lane (lead-1d0eo): no new types this session.\n- Grooming of all open work (lead-izfpk): ordering, not doing.\n- Draining the register pileup (lead-vx02q): work of its own.\n- The Framing-refinement rule (lead-ghulb): not needed to route."
  change: each no-go carries a reason clause, but the no-gos themselves are bead ids and shop shorthand ("the configuration lane", "the register pileup", "the Framing-refinement rule") a reader of the initiative alone cannot resolve, so the reason cannot be judged against what it excludes. Give each no-go a half-line saying what it is before the reason, or drop the ones that are just backlog items and not near-misses of this bet.
  decided: wobbly
- criterion: uncovered
  section: Feasibility and usability (against Appetite)
  quoted: "Feasible; the verified run is the risk. [...] The definitions fit one session; the example change delivered and verified through the new lane may not. (architect, 2026-09-04)" — against Appetite: "One working session of the lead shop, covering every ask recorded and routed on arrival, the route into discovery kept open, and the example change verified: definitions alone do not meet the measure."
  change: the appetite requires the example change verified within one session and says definitions alone do not meet the measure; the architect says the verified example change may not fit one session. The verdict "Feasible" does not say whether the bet is feasible within its appetite. Either the architect states feasibility against the appetite as written ("feasible within one session: uncertain, because ...") or the appetite is widened or the measure narrowed, so the authority bets on a consistent statement.
  decided: wobbly

Sections reported clean: For whom against scenario 2 (who, one measure, "Now 0", "Target 1", interaction type "conversational" — all present); Appetite against scenario 3's bound ("One working session of the lead shop"); Feasibility and usability against scenario 5 (architect verdict with reasons present; designer hypothesis present for the named interaction type); Decomposition against scenario 6 ("None: no Bounded Context is touched ... Cross-context flow: none"); scenario 7 (my count is roughly 480 words outside the Document History — under the bound but with little room; the bet — one session, spent on recorded and routed asks plus a small-change lane, for the example change reaching a verified result — is statable from Framing, For whom, and Appetite alone).

top_three:
1. For whom: replace "a related-to entry on the decision brief" with a what, or have the authority rule the example instance a what (scenario 4).
2. Feasibility vs Appetite: make the architect's verdict answer feasibility within the one-session appetite, since the appetite requires the verified example change and the architect says it may not fit (uncovered).
3. Framing: resolve the "entry-point" quote under the owner's no-exemption ruling — keep only the first quote, or the authority rules it a what (scenario 4).
